name: Spring Creek MX Park

soil.notes: Mix of sand sections (notably the sand whoops) and hardpack; billed as some of the richest soil on the circuit with strong traction. Rain makes the dirt thick and muddy.

layout.notes: In the Mississippi River valley by the creek. Steep downhills (steeper than TV shows), uphills, off-cambers, sand whoops into a triple; long fast first right narrows sharply and causes pileups.

conditions.dry: Strong traction; considered easy to set up compared with Southwick.
conditions.wet: Rain makes dirt thick; mud makes bikes hard to hold; tractors may not get onto wet sections.
conditions.late_day: Gets rougher through the day; distinct inside/outside lines form in fast turns on rough days; long right-hander always ruts deep.
conditions.watering_prep: Groomed and watered; crew preps heavily for nationals.
conditions.seasonal: Open practice on select Saturdays (about twice a month); MN OHV permit required. Pro national each July since 1983 (first pro event 1982).

rider_reports.says: Analyst: momentum through the first chicane and sand whoops decides whether you clear the triple; work with the track rather than muscling berms; rain before moto two caused crashes.
Analyst: sand whoops, big hills, off-cambers and hardpack with strong traction; easy to dial in; first turn invites contact.
Technique breakdown: keep weight back and front light in sand whoops, stand through downhills, point toes in to avoid catching ruts, use clutch on downhills, keep momentum in mud on a 250.
